findings: Four-input core unrolls compression rounds over transposed message words stored in stack offsets0..0xF0, with scratch0x100. Rotations16/8 use pshufb constants;12/7 use shifts/or. No arithmetic parity claim without execution.

Final block-loop jne depends on comparison before the vector core: intervening SIMD operations and mov preserve flags. This long-distance flag dependency is intentional source flow, not a demonstrated missing comparison.

Four-lane output is transposed back and stored as eight16-byte writes spanning128 bytes, then input pointer advances32 and output128. Counter low words add masked step4 and high words propagate unsigned carry via sign-bit xor/comparison.

After all complete groups, low remainder bits select2 then1. Two-input setup reads exactly four16-byte vectors from each64-byte block. Its seven-round loop and counter-lane shift connect to the previously read tail ending.

For zero inputs no output stores occur, though prologue still loads output pointer and prepares counters. For nonzero inputs block count must be positive and representable after shift6; full blocks and sufficient key/output buffers remain caller contracts.
Return restores RBP anchor and six callee-saved general registers. Source uses SSE4.1 pinsrd/pblendw/blendvps and SSSE3 pshufb; it is not SSE2-compatible merely because all vector registers are XMM.
Scalar32-byte in-place and64-byte XOF paths, full64-byte padded reads and constant sections were reviewed in v130. Windows variants still require separate ABI and source review.
